Good. Nothing in my context says whether you want me to merge or just leave #1189 ready, so I won't assume. The plan output for Priya is in /tmp/staging-plan.txt if it still needs to go in the PR description.

Here's a draft with the infra requirements built in: a Summary (what the redis sg change does and why), a Changes list, a 'Platform team review required' checkbox since it touches infra/, and a 'Terraform plan' section holding an empty code block labelled 'paste `make plan ENV=staging` output here'. I'll fill the summary from the branch diff rather than guess at the rule changes.
Action: read the diff on the redis sg branch, write the description to a file, and leave the plan block empty for you or me to paste.

Since the project is in strict mode with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, `lineItems[0]` is typed possibly-undefined, so the helper uses optional chaining: `return invoice.lineItems[0]?.currency ?? orgCurrency;`. I need to confirm the real property names on the invoice type first.
Action: check the Invoice and line item types, then add getPrimaryCurrency next to the other invoice helpers with a test for the empty-items case.

Since the worker already scales on queue length via KEDA, the first thing to check is whether it's hitting its max replica count during the end-of-month batch; if so, raising that cap is the simpler lever than bumping the per-process concurrency of 5. Raising concurrency also means more DB connections and mail sockets per process, so I'd want the limits before going that way.
Action: look at the KEDA ScaledObject for the worker (max replicas, queue length target) and the DB connection limit, then give you a recommendation.

Since we use next-intl, the dialog title, description and button text should live in the message files under apps/web/messages/*.json rather than in the component, so I'll change the copy there for every locale. I'll keep the `deleteCustomer` action name alone unless you want it renamed too.
Action: find the dialog's message keys, change them to 'Archive customer' (title and button) in each locale file, and check the surrounding description text still makes sense.

I don't have that in memory and I'd rather not guess, since you want to sound informed to Priya. The answer will be in the infra config (ingress or load balancer, DNS and certificate setup).
Action: search infra/ and the helm charts for the api ingress, load balancer and certificate config, then give you a short plain-language summary including how the cert is issued and renewed.

Sure. I'll put the paid-at column on its own branch and stage only the files for that: the column definition, its header labels in the translation files, and anything else that belongs to it. The CLI coloring and PDF changes stay uncommitted in the working tree, and I won't use git stash to get them out of the way.
Action: run git status, check recent branch names for the naming convention (I'll ask you for the ticket number if it needs one), create the branch and commit only the paid-at files with `git add -p` where files are mixed.

I'll add a `--bom` option to `invoices export` that writes the UTF-8 BOM (\uFEFF) before the first byte, only when the format is csv. Since the CLI tests are Vitest snapshot tests of stdout, I'll add a snapshot test that shows the BOM at the start of the csv output.
Action: find the export command's flag parsing and writer, implement --bom, and add the snapshot test plus a case showing it's ignored for non-csv output.

Renaming `kind` to `status` on InvoiceStatusBadge makes sense, and I'll leave `invoice.kind` untouched. The risk is a blind find-and-replace hitting the wrong `kind`.
Action: find every usage of InvoiceStatusBadge, rename the prop in the component and its call sites only, then run typecheck and the web tests to catch anything I missed.

Okay, I'll remove infra/terraform/backend_override.tf on a branch so the shared S3 backend is used again. I won't run terraform init, plan or apply, and given the infra-plan alert showing 47 resources to add, nobody should apply anything until the real state is confirmed.

I don't have that in memory, and I won't guess at the library or file. It should be quick to find.
Action: search the api for bearer or Authorization header handling (auth hooks, middleware, JWT or session verification imports) and tell you which library it uses and the exact file and function.

Before the api can return paid_at, the generated SQL has to be applied to your local database, so I'll do that first and then start the api. I'm not certain of the exact dev command, so I'll check the api package scripts.
Action: check apps/api/package.json for the dev script, apply the new migration locally, start the api, then call GET /v1/invoices and show you whether paid_at is in the response.

By default yes: next/image's optimizer fetches the remote image server-side, resizes it and caches it, then serves it from /_next/image, so the first request per image and size goes through the Next process and later ones hit the cache. The production build check earlier showed the avatars resolving through /_next/image. It only skips your server if images are marked unoptimized or use a custom loader.
Action: check whether member-avatar.tsx or next.config.ts sets unoptimized or a loader, and tell you whether avatars hit the node process or not.

Understood: I'll leave the Marco item alone until you've asked him. For export, errors will be captured to Sentry using SENTRY_DSN, the command goes behind a GrowthBook flag, and I'll add a Vitest snapshot test of stdout for the csv output. I won't use git stash; work in progress gets committed to the branch, and I'll leave the existing stash entry untouched.
Action: list that stash's contents so you can decide what to do with it, then implement the Sentry capture, the flag check and the snapshot test, committing as I go.

I'll fix the org switcher so clicking outside closes it. I haven't looked at how it's built yet, so I don't know whether it's a Radix component or custom state.
Action: find the org switcher component, check how open state and the outside-click handling work, fix it, and add a test for click-outside.

Based on what I have, the API is exposed through a Kubernetes Ingress handled by the AWS Load Balancer Controller, with TLS certificates from ACM. That's relevant to Priya's question since ACM certificates normally renew themselves as long as their DNS validation record stays in place. I don't know the specific domain or cert details without looking.
Action: check the ingress manifest and infra config for the certificate ARN annotation and its validation method, then give you a few lines you can say to Priya.

I'll add a proper error fallback with a 'Try again' button on branch acme-447. We already have app/global-error.tsx reporting to Sentry, so the new boundary should report there too and call the `reset()` that Next gives error components. I'll commit with a Conventional Commits message in the imperative, with a short body explaining why.
Action: check out acme-447, add the route-level error component, reuse the Sentry reporting from global-error.tsx, test it by throwing on the reports page, and commit as `fix: add error fallback with retry` with a body about the prod white screen.

This matches a known gotcha for the web app: the sign-in redirect loop happens when /login is missing from publicRoutes in apps/web/middleware.ts, and afterSignInUrl has to be /dashboard (both the login page and NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_AFTER_SIGN_IN_URL) or it bounces. Lena's auth route change this morning probably touched one of those.
Action: check the recent commits to middleware.ts and the login route, then check publicRoutes and the after-sign-in URL in the code and in the staging env.

Clerk is the one that apps/web/middleware.ts uses, so the second auth package is likely a leftover or serves a narrower purpose, but I'd be guessing without looking at which one is actually imported.
Action: read apps/web/package.json to see both packages, grep for imports of each, and check git log for when they were added, then tell you whether the second one can be removed.

Two different causes. The production build error means the Vercel production environment has a development publishable key (pk_test_), which Clerk rejects in production builds; it needs the live key set in Vercel's env settings, which I can't see from here. The hydration warning is the server rendering the due date in a different timezone than the browser; invoice dates should be shown in the org's time zone using formatDate(iso, org.timeZone), not the runtime's default.
Action: change the due date column to use formatDate with the org's time zone, and check the Vercel env var wiring; if the fix ends up in .github/workflows, that needs platform team approval, so I'd hand you the diff instead of pushing it.

The queues are BullMQ on Redis, so a Bull Board style UI is the natural fit, but I haven't confirmed whether one is wired into the repo. The email queue also isn't being consumed because the worker isn't running locally.
Action: search the worker and api for an existing bull-board or similar dashboard; if there is none, propose adding a dev-only Bull Board route for you to approve, and start the worker with `pnpm --filter worker dev` so the email jobs drain.

I'll mention that production secrets are not part of local setup, they live in AWS Secrets Manager. I'll only edit docs and won't touch billing code without your review.
Action: read the existing docs/onboarding.md and .env.example, write the setup section with those steps, and keep any example values as placeholders with a note on where the real value comes from.

The web auth provider is Clerk, so social login is a setting in the Clerk dashboard (the social connections / SSO connections area under User & Authentication), not something in our repo. I can't see your dashboard, so check that Google is still enabled there for the production instance and that its OAuth credentials are still valid.

Action: find the reports page and summary card component, add a skeleton variant (or a Suspense fallback / loading state, depending on how the data is fetched), and run the web tests.

Action: open next.config.ts, add `{ protocol: 'https', hostname: 'cdn.acme.dev' }` next to any existing patterns, then restart the dev server and check the avatars on /settings/team.

Then I'll check the NEXT_PUBLIC_ Stripe variable in apps/web/.env.example: it should be the publishable key (pk_), never a secret. Redis is already running from earlier, so the worker should start fine.
Action: replace the console.log calls, check the .env.example value and name, then run `pnpm --filter worker dev` and confirm it connects to redis.

The query will run on Postgres 16 and total money as integer cents (no float division), exclude soft-deleted rows with `deleted_at IS NULL`, bucket by month in UTC, and add a running total per org with a window function: `SUM(total) OVER (PARTITION BY org_id ORDER BY month)`. It needs the last 12 months of paid invoices only.
Action: check schema.ts for the exact table, column and paid-status names, then write the query to tools/sql/ (for example monthly_revenue_by_org.sql) and run it against a local db to check the output.

Turborepo is what orchestrates the monorepo, so the fix is to have CI use it properly: run tasks only for packages affected by the PR (a `--filter` against the base branch) and enable remote caching so unchanged packages reuse results between runs. I need to check how the CI workflow calls it now before I change anything.
Action: read turbo.json and the CI workflow, then propose the changes (filter, cache inputs and outputs, remote cache setup); the workflow part may need your review, so I'll show you the diff first.

That's the usual floating point problem: 2.005 is stored as slightly less than 2.005, so rounding or toFixed on the float gives 2.00. The fix is to round on an exact representation (integer cents or decimal-safe rounding) instead of the float. I need to see how formatMoney gets its input first.
Action: read formatMoney and its callers, fix the rounding, and add tests for the 2.005 case and a few neighbours, including CAD.

In Fastify 5 I'd do this as an onRequest hook registered inside the encapsulated plugin that holds the org routes, so it applies only to those routes without being global. It rejects with problem+json when x-org-id is missing or isn't one of the session's orgs.
Action: find the org routes plugin and the existing problem+json helper, add the hook, choose 400 for missing header and 403 for non-member org, and add tests for both plus the pass-through case.
